# Boundary-Aware NL2SQL: Integrating Reliability through Hybrid Reward and Data Synthesis

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#bar-sql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.10318v1) · arXiv:2601.10318v1, 15 January 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 26 pages, Sections 1-6, Appendices A-C, full synthesis/validation/inference prompts, reward equations, Tables 1-4 and Algorithm 1.

## Research question

Enterprise SQL generators may force answers despite missing metric definitions, dimensions or user-specified constraints.

## Method

Mutates business-grounded seed questions into eight tasks, synthesizes target-conditioned rationales, then fine-tunes Qwen3-1.7B with supervised learning and GRPO. Rewards combine SQL execution/structure, response similarity, output format and length.

## Evaluation

Ent-SQL-Bench is a 1,262-instance held-out sample of the same synthetic enterprise corpus. SQL tasks use execution agreement; clarification/refusal targets use three GPT-4o judgments. Ablations remove auxiliary reward terms while preserving the primary outcome rewards.

## What the results support

The reported macro-average improves after training, including non-SQL response categories. Results support task-conditioned behavior within the studied corpus, without testing user replies or successful clarification-to-SQL completion.

## Limits and qualifications

Target-conditioned rationales are constructed explanations, not evidence of faithful internal reasoning. No cross-domain or independent user study supports general enterprise-readiness claims. Main training descriptions disagree on five versus ten SFT epochs, and the source omits confidence intervals or seed variability for its headline gains.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Directly relevant boundary-aware training baseline; distinguish its outcome scoring from verified reasoning, interactive recovery and deployment reliability.
